heroLead: Castle Valley sits east of Moab beneath the La Sal Mountains, a small residential community where the surface has changed dramatically while the mineral estate underneath has mostly stayed with the original owning families.
intro: Castle Valley has grown as a quiet residential enclave known for its striking red-rock scenery, but that surface transformation has little bearing on the underlying oil and gas mineral estate, much of which was severed from the surface generations before the current homes were built. Interests here generally tie into the broader Paradox Basin trend that includes the Cane Creek shale development southwest of Moab, though this specific area sits further from the active core.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Castle Valley directly. Send us your deed or division order and we will confirm the legal description and any associated production before quoting a number.

sections.heading: Surface development, separate mineral history
paragraphs: It is common for a Castle Valley property owner today to have no idea that the mineral rights under their land were sold or reserved decades before the current residential development took shape, since the surface transaction that brought them to the valley likely never touched the mineral estate at all. If you are the heir of a family that held minerals here before the area's residential growth, that interest is a separate asset from any surface property and can be evaluated and sold independently.

sections.heading: Distance from the active Cane Creek core
paragraphs: Castle Valley sits outside the immediate Cane Creek development area southwest of Moab, so interests here generally reflect quieter, less actively drilled acreage. That affects the number, but it does not mean an interest here has no value, particularly if there is any historical production or nearby permitting activity to point to. We check both before making an offer.

faqs.question: I live in Castle Valley but I'm not sure I own the minerals under my property. How do I check?
faqs.answer: We can review your deed and the recorder's records to confirm whether your family retained mineral rights or whether they were severed before you acquired the surface.

faqs.question: Is Castle Valley part of the active Cane Creek development area?
faqs.answer: Generally not the core, though it sits within the broader Paradox Basin. We confirm actual production tied to your interest before quoting.

faqs.question: Can I sell my mineral interest without affecting my home or property?
faqs.answer: Yes, a mineral sale is separate from your surface property and does not affect your home.
